  "markdown_report": "At 10% progress, select **a conservative competitive-negative curriculum for the existing prefix/suffix NextItNet objective**, conditional on first establishing the prefix/suffix reference. This changes sampling while retaining one model and weak recent-suffix supervision; improvement remains untested.

Three starting-point insights guide the experiment. First, shared prefix/suffix parameters permit one-checkpoint deployment. Cropping assumes the retained context supports the same target, so its auxiliary weight should remain weak. NextItNet’s finite receptive field also makes sufficiently long suffixes redundant under matching padding, local normalization, and deterministic computation. Second, strong uniform training-audit rankings coexist with weaker competitive rankings: Movies’ hit rate falls from 0.98965 to 0.72450 against prefix-lexical competitors. This motivates discrimination experiments, without establishing embedding collapse or generalization. Third, users reject both functionally unsuitable related products and entertainment matches missing specific qualities. Competitive supervision targets these distinct failures, but interaction labels establish neither compatibility nor mood.

Three literature insights refine the direction. AHNS motivates positive-relative hardness; a fixed rank band ignores positive scores and does not reproduce AHNS. R²NS motivates warm-up and stochastic selection, while warning about fluctuating hardness and limited coverage from small random pools. Correcting the LogQ Correction distinguishes estimation from deliberate sampling bias; uniform logQ correction is inappropriate after mining. Supervised-augmentation research directly precedes cropping, while MARS motivates finer textual distinctions without validating a scratch encoder here.

The framework separates three directions: **candidate discrimination**, **context selection**, and **item representation**. Sampling changes gradient competition; cropping changes accessible evidence; text changes item features. Separate trials preserve interpretability.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, out of ten; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Five assessments |
|---|---|
| Competitive-negative curriculum, selected [AHNS, R²NS] | O 3: +targeted transfer, −established sampling; P 6: +reusable experiment, −false negatives and benchmark mismatch; U 6: +functional/taste competition, −no intent labels; M 8: +competitive discrimination, −training-only evidence; D 6: +unchanged inference, −causal masking and mining cost |
| Timestamp-conditioned causal tap attenuation [drift-aware subsequences] | O 5: +NextItNet adaptation, −existing context gates; P 7: +context control, −unidentified boundaries; U 7: +stale interests, −compatibility unresolved; M 4: +context hypothesis, −no measured drift failure; D 7: +one network, −causal tap rewrite |
| Joint scratch title encoder [MARS] | O 3: +permitted adaptation, −standard fusion; P 6: +fine distinctions, −sparse supervision; U 8: +functional and musical descriptors, −incomplete text; M 6: +lexical discrimination, −overlap shortcuts; D 6: +small encoder, −tokenization/export cost |

For the selected idea, warm up uniformly, then introduce at most 20% stochastic negatives from pool ranks 9–64. Share candidates across complete-prefix and suffix losses. Preserve uniform coverage and record target-relative margins: rank bands alone do not maintain constant difficulty. This explicitly targets broad functional matches displacing concrete complements and broad entertainment matches missing specific taste; benefits remain hypotheses. Timestamp gates and text remain later alternatives.

Compare against unchanged sampling. If suffix supervision is unestablished, first compare baseline, duplicate-prefix auxiliary loss, and genuine context-truncation auxiliary loss with matched updates and reported GPU costs. Compute receptive field from every temporal convolution; a suffix must remove accessible evidence to test truncation.

Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve four categories, seeds, budgets, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. Deploy one complete-prefix pass. Repeat the frozen competitive audit as supporting evidence, preserving definitions and unavailable fields. Track sampling coverage, margins, gradients, and popularity shortcuts; report validation strata only if supplied by the unchanged host. No results or execution are claimed.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Replace a small fraction of uniform negatives in the established shared-parameter prefix/suffix NextItNet objective with progressively introduced stochastic competitive negatives. Treat the fixed pool-rank band as a simplified training hypothesis, distinct from AHNS and R²NS. Preserve one jointly trained NextItNet and one selected checkpoint per category, with complete-prefix-only inference.",
    "motivation": "The current diagnosis shows strong fitted-training ranking against uniform candidates but weaker ranking against popular and lexical competitors, especially in Movies_and_TV and Industrial_and_Scientific. The sampler explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broadly related but functionally unsuitable products displacing concrete matches, and entertainment recommendations matching broad genre or era while missing specific qualities. These mechanisms are plausible only where next-item supervision distinguishes the alternatives; the sampler supplies no compatibility, quantity, mood, or current-purpose labels. Mining may instead emphasize popular items, substitutes, or ambiguous positives. Current Electronics pairwise errors are 0.20%; the older 6.38% figure must not guide this experiment. Strong training discrimination and prior combined_score values do not establish improvement under the pinned validation protocol.",
    "implementation_notes": "Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing its absent source. Retain the NextItNet backbone, optimizer, family-specific sample_batch target alignment, prefix construction, and existing weak suffix coefficient. The experimental change is negative sampling alone. If the supplied cold start does not yet implement the starting prefix/suffix objective, establish that objective as the reference before adding mining. No filesystem inspection, training, validation, or literature verification was performed for this report; descriptions of related work rely on the supplied search material.

Validate the suffix reference before interpreting it as context regularization. For stride-one causal convolutions, compute maximum receptive-field span R = 1 + sum((kernel_size - 1) * dilation), counting every temporal convolution along the deepest path. Residual shortcuts do not enlarge that maximum. A suffix retaining all positions capable of influencing its selected output is redundant when positions, padding semantics, local normalization, and deterministic computation match. Biases or improperly masked padding can break equivalence. Global pooling, sequence-wide normalization, or additional context-dependent modules require separate dependency analysis. Shorter suffixes remove accessible evidence but may no longer sufficiently support the target. Cropping is target-preserving by construction only in its label assignment; semantic sufficiency is an assumption.

If this reference needs establishment, compare the corrected baseline, a duplicate-full-prefix auxiliary CE control, and a recent-suffix auxiliary CE variant. Use the same target, candidate IDs, valid output positions, minibatch stream, and existing weak auxiliary coefficient. A duplicate loss with coefficient lambda becomes (1 + lambda) times the original loss when outputs coincide, so it changes gradient scale; retain it as an optimization-scale control and report this fact. Independent dropout masks introduce another regularization difference. Test deterministic prefix/suffix equivalence in evaluation mode, and document training dropout behavior. Choose suffix length below the measured receptive field when feasible; report the fraction of supervised examples for which cropping actually removes accessible evidence. Do not launch a broad suffix sweep automatically. Match optimizer updates and validation schedule, report processed positions and GPU seconds, and acknowledge that equal updates and equal compute generally cannot both be maintained.

For the sampling trial, use 99 unique negatives per supported target, with epochs 0–4 entirely uniform. During epochs 5–19, increase the competitive fraction linearly from 0.20/15 to 0.20; retain 0.20 afterward. These are prespecified initial settings, not established optima. For K available negative slots, use floor(fraction * K) competitive slots; this gives at most 19 competitive negatives when K = 99. Define pool size 256 and the eligible score-rank band 9–64, inclusive, with descending score and ascending mapped item ID tie breaking. Sample uniformly without replacement within that band, then fill remaining slots uniformly without replacement from eligible IDs excluding already selected candidates. Reduce K to the eligible-catalog size and log such cases; require at least one negative for a supported CE example. Do not silently substitute repeated negatives.

A fixed rank band does not reproduce AHNS's positive-aware score criterion or R²NS's global retrieval, random candidates, and shrinking hard subset. Pool ranks fluctuate with pool composition, score gaps, and training stage. Start with this simpler sampler because progress is early; reserve a target-relative hardness rule or broader retrieval for a separate later trial if measured margins and coverage show the rank band is inadequate. Hardest-only sampling is an optional separate control if budget permits, never an inference component or automatically launched sweep. The main comparison remains uniform sampling versus the prespecified curriculum.

Preserve autoregressive all-position supervision. Compute complete-sequence features once for each sampled batch, then flatten positions with nonzero sequence input and positive target. Each position's feature must depend only on its visible prefix, with the positive being the next item. Do not insert the target into its own input context or shift to final-position-only training. Mine from detached current-model features and item scores, then recompute selected candidate logits with gradients through the original features and item embeddings. Use the baseline's actual scoring function, including any trained normalization, projection, or bias. Matrix multiplication against sampled item embeddings is equivalent only if predict_score implements that dot product; otherwise vectorize the actual scoring head.

For efficient mining, draw one uniform pool of up to 256 distinct nonpadding training-catalog IDs per training batch using the dedicated sampler RNG. Reuse that pool across feature-row chunks. Per row, mask its current target and all items visible in its causal prefix before ranking. This replaces the previous computationally expensive suggestion to re-encode every prefix separately; shared pools create correlated row-level draws, which should be documented. Rows with fewer eligible pool members use the available portion of ranks 9–64 and fill any missing competitive slots uniformly. The underlying eligible set for uniform filling remains the complete mapped training catalog after row exclusions. Record fallback rates and effective competitive fractions. Build prefix membership from the actual sequence and positions, including known truncated-away context only if the baseline already supplies it causally; never assume unavailable earlier history.

Do not use later training events, validation labels, or test labels to filter candidates. The suggestion to exclude all observed training positives would, at intermediate autoregressive positions, reveal future interactions. Exclude causally observed prefix positives instead. If the corrected baseline has another exclusion policy, document the discrepancy and establish a matched uniform reference under the exact same policy before attributing effects to hardness. Prefix exclusion can suppress repeat-consumption alternatives; this limitation remains even though the actual target is always retained. Unobserved candidates are not verified negatives, and false-negative rates cannot be measured directly here. Later-training-positive overlap, if retained in the frozen diagnostic audit, remains retrospective diagnostic information and must not influence sampling.

Mine from detached scores produced by the same training forward pass, preserving the baseline's training mode and dropout. This avoids a second complete encoding and makes no claim that mining scores equal deterministic deployment scores. A separate eval-mode mining pass would be a different, more expensive protocol; it is not part of this initial configuration. Chunk valid feature rows to bound score storage and compute prefix exclusions without constructing a B-by-L-by-catalog tensor. If candidate columns are chunked, merge the globally best 64 eligible pool candidates before applying the rank band; selecting independently within chunks changes the sampler. Chunking limits temporary memory, not total dot products. Recompute selected logits with gradients; candidate selection itself remains detached.

Use identical target and candidate IDs for full-prefix and suffix CE. Keep the inherited full-prefix loss dominant and its reduction unchanged: average each branch over its declared supported positions, then combine with the inherited weak coefficient. If suffix examples are supported only for a subset, record that support rather than changing loss scale silently. A per-position suffix implementation requires correctly aligned cropped examples for those positions; cropping one batch row once does not automatically implement every position's recent-suffix auxiliary objective. Keep the established suffix implementation unchanged in the sampling comparison. Candidates mined from a full prefix may be ambiguous for a truncated suffix, so monitor branch losses and retain the weak weight rather than asserting consistency.

Optimize uncorrected sampled-candidate cross-entropy. This is a deliberately biased competitive ranking objective, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Do not apply uniform-proposal logQ correction to mined candidates or claim the mixture has a simple uniform proposal probability. The always-included positive and the adaptively sampled negatives require different treatment for a genuine estimator, which is outside this trial. Target-conditioned lexical-oracle audit candidates remain diagnostic only. Neither lexical scores nor popularity scores contribute to deployed rankings.

Keep maximum epochs 200 and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch, preprocessing seed 0, and training seed 42. Use a dedicated sampling RNG seeded 42, separate from model initialization, dropout, and diagnostic RNGs. Record RNG libraries and states, batch size, sequence length, precision, optimizer settings, negative counts, actual suffix coefficient and policy, architecture configuration, validation schedule, checkpoint rule, library versions, and GPU model from the supplied source. Predeclare compute allocation and record realized updates if the shared time budget stops training. One GPU is used per trial. Training, pool scoring, diagnostics, debugging, export verification, and failed trials consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance; four concurrent slots do not expand it. Reserve budget for the matched reference before optional controls. No performance claim or completed experiment is implied.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl with existing routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Select exclusively by the pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negative candidates, and evaluation seed 42. Keep the inherited validation and checkpoint schedule, log every validation query, and report the four category outcomes. Preserve one selected checkpoint per category using the host's existing selection policy; do not invent a new category-wise or joint checkpoint rule. Freeze the selected configuration before the separate held-out evaluation. Do not access hidden tests, other trials, their checkpoints, extra datasets, or pretrained weights.

Record sampled positive-minus-negative score margins, the fraction of selected negatives outranking positives, selected pool ranks, unique-item coverage, training-frequency distributions, fallback rates, competitive fractions, loss, bounded gradient norms, GPU time, and peak memory. For sampled CE, detached per-logit derivatives are p_negative for a negative and p_positive - 1 for the positive; record these with the loss reduction stated. A separately reported pairwise softplus loss or its derivative is a diagnostic surrogate, not the optimized objective. Raw margins depend on score scale. Compare score–log-frequency Spearman correlation on a frozen permitted training-prefix/catalog sample with identical support across trials. Frequency and title similarity are shortcut or false-negative risk indicators, not preference labels. Popularity-stratified validation HR@10 is available only if the unchanged host supplies the needed outputs; otherwise mark it unavailable. Do not alter the evaluator or replace the primary metric.

Repeat the frozen competitive training audit with identical manifests, candidate sets, definitions, and support whenever the existing adapter permits. Its fitted-target rankings are not holdout evidence. All supplied audits internally lacked category identity and used category index 0; do not claim the documented category-aware seed scheme was realized or silently relabel old artifacts. Preserve this limitation in comparisons. Conditional paired-user bootstrap intervals exclude training-seed uncertainty, adaptive selection, and shared-item dependence. Stronger audit discrimination alone is insufficient for selection. Mining may overfit fitted targets, training popularity, or repeatedly sampled items, and it may hurt the benchmark's uniform-candidate objective or full-catalog usefulness. Low pairwise error rates and embedding scores near 0.5 do not justify a collapse intervention.

Keep ModelView.model as the actual trained nn.Module and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors; training-time multi-negative tensors remain internal and must not break that interface. Diagnostics score the actual trained features and distinguish fitted-training ranks from validation HR@10. Preserve unavailable validation/reload fields unless genuinely measured through an appropriate separate interface. Stable user identities are unavailable for ordinary loader rows; do not invent user-level uncertainty from them.

Preserve the native twenty-real-training-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendation process, five users per category. When native outputs support it, track functionally unsuitable broad matches and entertainment-specific mismatches separately, rank concrete complements or specific taste matches against merely related choices, and distinguish explicit rejections from uncertain judgments. Do not derive numeric rejection rates from qualitative summaries. Improved competitive margins do not demonstrate resolution of duplicate functionality, quantity, compatibility, or mood. Only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are available; generic review/rating/category/price/store schemas and simulator traits remain unavailable. This sampler requires no metadata pipeline.

Inference remains architecturally unchanged: one complete-prefix pass, exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category, no mining, suffix-score fusion, checkpoint averaging, independent experts, or separately fitted score additions. Preserve the predictor writer and generated working/predict.py architecture, mappings, configuration, and checkpoint consistency. Reuse the final sequence feature across candidate chunks. For left padding, locate the final nonzero position by positional maximum, never count-1; handle empty histories explicitly through the corrected baseline policy. Verify causal target alignment, finite outputs, padding behavior, candidate mapping, all four routes, and generated-predictor reload score agreement on identical permitted inputs in eval mode. In-memory view/network agreement does not establish deployment parity. The source, concrete constructor, inherited hyperparameters, suffix policy, validation/checkpoint schedule, and host interfaces are absent from this prompt, so the pseudocode remains an integration specification rather than a runnable train.py or an independently reproducible completed experiment.",
    "pseudocode": "CONFIG = {
    'negative_count': 99,
    'pool_size': 256,
    'warmup_epochs': 5,
    'ramp_epochs': 15,
    'maximum_competitive_fraction': 0.20,
    'eligible_pool_rank_first': 9,
    'eligible_pool_rank_last': 64,
}
# Baseline-specific helpers below are integration placeholders.
# Before adding mining, establish the supplied prefix/suffix reference.
# Compute R from every causal temporal convolution and record whether each
# suffix removes evidence accessible to its corresponding full-prefix output.
# If needed, compare baseline / duplicate-prefix auxiliary / suffix auxiliary
# in separate trials; never combine independently trained trial outputs.

for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
    model = supplied_corrected_nextitnet_cold_start(seed=42)
    sampler_rng = dedicated_rng(seed=42)
    for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        if epoch < 5:
            fraction = 0.0
        else:
            fraction = 0.20 * min((epoch - 4) / 15.0, 1.0)
        for batch_index in range(200):
            batch = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
            sequence, positive = aligned_training_inputs_and_next_targets(batch)
            model.train()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)  # B,L,D; causal, padding-safe
            rows = supported_positions(sequence.ne(0) & positive.ne(0))
            # Every selected feature uses only its own prefix.
            shared_pool = None
            if fraction > 0:
                shared_pool = sample_unique(
                    mapped_nonpadding_training_catalog,
                    min(256, catalog_size), sampler_rng)
            selected_ids = []
            for row_chunk in chunk(rows, recorded_row_chunk_size):
                h = features_at(features, row_chunk)
                y = positive_at(positive, row_chunk)
                # Exclusions are row-specific, causal, and identical in controls.
                visible = visible_prefix_ids(sequence, row_chunk)
                eligible = catalog_excluding_padding_target_and_visible(y, visible)
                K = minimum_per_row(99, eligible.size)
                require_or_report_no_negative_rows(K)
                competitive = empty_per_row_selection()
                if fraction > 0:
                    with no_grad():
                        pool_scores = actual_score_head(
                            model, h.detach(), shared_pool)
                        pool_scores = mask_target_and_visible_prefix(
                            pool_scores, shared_pool, y, visible)
                        # If columns are chunked, merge a GLOBAL top-64 per row.
                        ranked = finite_eligible_top64(
                            shared_pool, pool_scores,
                            tie_break='mapped item ID ascending')
                        moderate = ranked[:, 8:64]  # eligible ranks 9..64
                        requested = floor(fraction * K)
                        competitive = sample_unique_per_row(
                            moderate, min_per_row(requested, moderate.size),
                            sampler_rng)
                uniform = sample_unique_per_row(
                    eligible.minus(competitive),
                    K - competitive.size, sampler_rng)
                candidates = concatenate_per_row(y, competitive, uniform)
                # Mask any padded candidate slots for genuinely small catalogs.
                selected_ids.append((row_chunk, candidates))
                log_sampling_support_ranks_margins_coverage_and_fallbacks(...)

            # Recompute selected logits WITH gradients through original features
            # and the actual trained candidate representation/scoring pathway.
            full_loss = supported_mean_cross_entropy(
                model, features, positive, selected_ids, positive_index=0)
            # Preserve the ESTABLISHED per-position suffix implementation.
            # It uses the same target/candidates and documented branch support.
            suffix_loss, suffix_support = established_suffix_auxiliary_ce(
                model, batch, selected_ids)
            loss = full_loss + inherited_weak_suffix_weight * suffix_loss
            baseline_optimizer_zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            record_bounded_gradient_diagnostics_if_prespecified(...)
            baseline_optimizer_step()
        apply_existing_validation_and_checkpoint_policy()
        record_updates_positions_GPU_seconds_and_validation_queries(...)
    export_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(category)
    verify_generated_predictor_reload_scores_and_category_routing(...)

# Deployment: one selected model per category; no mining or suffix fusion.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
nonempty = last.ge(0)
final_features = features[nonempty, last[nonempty]]
for candidate_chunk in candidate_chunks:
    scores_for_chunk = model.predict_score(final_features, candidate_chunk)
# Explicitly apply the corrected baseline policy to empty rows.
# Keep DiagnosisProbe, ModelView, diagnostic loader and interpreter contracts.
# Report unmeasured validation strata/reload diagnostics as unavailable.
# Select exclusively by the unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.",
